questions.question: A disease like COVID-19 is a kind of:
questions.solution:
COVID-19 is classified as a Zoonotic disease, which means it is caused by germs that spread between animals and people.
  • The virus responsible, SARS-CoV-2, is believed to have originated in bats before potentially passing through an intermediate host to humans.
  • Other examples of zoonotic diseases include Rabies, Ebola, and Bird Flu.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Ribosomes?

Statement A: Ribosomes have no membrane.

Statement B: Digestive hydrolytic enzymes are present in Ribosomes.

Statement C: These are called suicidal bags.

Statement D: Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis.
questions.option_1: Only statements A, B and C
questions.solution:
Statements A and D are correct regarding Ribosomes.
  • Statement A: Ribosomes are unique because they are not membrane-bound, allowing them to exist in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
  • Statement D: Their primary function is protein synthesis (translation).
  • Correction: Digestive enzymes and 'suicidal bag' characteristics (Statements B and C) describe Lysosomes, not ribosomes.

questions.question: Constipation could be a sign that the person in suffering from a lack of ___________.
questions.solution:
Constipation is frequently a sign of a lack of Dietary Fibre in one's diet.
  • Fibre adds bulk to the stool and absorbs water, which helps waste move smoothly through the digestive tract.
  • High-fibre foods include whole grains, legumes, fruits, and vegetables.

questions.question: Gluten formation is observed in various foods like pasta, noodles, pizzas, and bread. Gluten occurs when two specific proteins are mixed with water. Name the two proteins responsible for gluten formation.
questions.solution:
Gluten is formed when the two proteins Glutenin and Gliadin are mixed with water and kneaded.
  • Gliadin provides the dough with its stickiness and extensibility, while Glutenin provides strength and elasticity.
  • This protein network is what gives bread its chewy texture and allows it to trap gases during rising.

questions.question: The major carbohydrate of milk is
questions.solution:
The primary carbohydrate found in milk is Lactose, often referred to as 'milk sugar.'
  • It is a disaccharide composed of one molecule of glucose and one molecule of galactose.
  • The enzyme lactase is required by the body to break it down during digestion.

questions.question: Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are also called ____________.
questions.solution:
Fats and carbohydrates are known as energy-giving foods.
  • Carbohydrates provide the body's main and immediate source of fuel.
  • Fats serve as a concentrated, long-term energy reserve.
  • Note: Proteins are termed 'body-building foods' as they are essential for growth and tissue repair.

questions.question: Which part of a flower develops into a seed?
questions.solution:
The Ovule is the part of a flower that develops into a seed after fertilization.
  • Meanwhile, the Ovary (the part of the pistil containing the ovules) typically matures into the fruit.

questions.question: Which organelle contains ribosomal RNA and is involved in the production of ribosomes?
questions.solution:
The Nucleolus is a dense region within the nucleus where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is synthesized.
  • It is responsible for assembling the subunits that make up ribosomes, which then exit the nucleus to begin protein production.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about nutrients are correct?

Statement A: C, H, O, N, P and K are macro nutrients.

Statement B: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo are micronutrients.

Statement C: Micronutrients are not essential for our body.
questions.option_3: All statements A, B and C
questions.solution:
Statements A and B are correct.
  • Macronutrients (C, H, O, N, P, K) are required by plants/humans in large quantities.
  • Micronutrients (Fe, Mn, Ni, Co, Mo) are needed in very small amounts.
  • Correction: Statement C is incorrect because micronutrients are absolutely essential; their deficiency can lead to severe physiological disorders or death.

questions.question: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in teenagers. Here body weight:
questions.solution:
In Anorexia Nervosa, a person's body weight loses drastically.
  • Individuals with this disorder severely restrict their calorie intake, leading to dangerously low body weight and potential organ failure.

questions.question:
Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by _________.

a) an abnormally heavy body weight

b) an intense fear of losing weight

c) a distorted perception of weight

d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
questions.solution:
Anorexia Nervosa is characterized by a distorted perception of weight (c) and excessive exercise/dieting to lose weight (d).
  • Even when underweight, individuals often perceive themselves as 'fat' and have an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.question: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
questions.solution:
The key nutrients that trigger Eutrophication are Phosphorus and Nitrogen.
  • Runoff from fertilizers and sewage introduces high levels of these nutrients into water bodies, fueling the massive growth of algae.

questions.question: What do you call the body cavity that is lined by mesoderm?
questions.solution:
A Coelom is a fluid-filled body cavity that is completely lined by mesoderm.
  • Animals possessing this true body cavity are called Coelomates (e.g., Annelids, Mollusks, and Chordates).
  • Note: Triploblasts refers to animals with three germ layers, and Diploblasts to those with two.

questions.question: When the body is deprived of energy from food, which of the following tissues is used to feed on its own?
questions.solution:
When the body is deprived of external food sources, it begins to feed on its own Adipose tissue (fat tissue).
  • The body breaks down stored triglycerides in fat cells to produce energy. Once fat reserves are depleted, the body may begin breaking down muscle protein.

questions.question: Which of the following is the role of fibre in the diet?
questions.solution:
The primary role of fibre is promoting digestion and bowel regularity.
  • Fibre is not digested by the human body; instead, it passes through the system, cleaning the digestive tract and preventing constipation.

questions.question: In the case of reptiles, their heart is not properly divided in to four chambers i.e., it consists of two auricles and an incompletely divided ventricle. Which of the following is an example.
questions.solution:
The Crocodile is the exception mentioned in the context of the question's premise.
  • While most reptiles (snakes, lizards, turtles) have a three-chambered heart with an incomplete ventricle, Crocodiles possess a four-chambered heart, similar to birds and mammals.

questions.question: Which of the following options represents the correct flow of energy in an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct flow of energy in an ecosystem is: Sunlight $ ightarrow$ Producers $ ightarrow$ Herbivores $ ightarrow$ Carnivores.
  • Producers (plants) capture sunlight, herbivores eat the plants, and carnivores eat the herbivores. Energy is lost as heat at each step.

questions.question: What is the term for the gradual, sequential changes in species composition in an ecosystem over time?
questions.solution:
Ecological Succession is the term for the gradual and sequential changes in species composition in a given area over time.
  • It usually starts with pioneer species (like lichens) and ends with a stable climax community.

questions.question: How does salt contribute to the preservation of food?
questions.option_2: By inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis.
questions.option_3: By reducing the pH of the food.
questions.solution:
Salt preserves food by inhibiting microbial growth through osmosis.
  • When food is salted, water is drawn out of the microbial cells (plasmolysis), making it impossible for bacteria or fungi to survive and multiply.

questions.question: In a food chain of Algae-Shrimp-Fish-Bird, if the energy available at the bird is 4 kJ, then the energy available at the shrimp is:
questions.solution:
Based on the 10% Law of energy transfer, the energy available at the shrimp is 400 kJ.
  • If the Bird (Top) has 4 kJ, the Fish (Level below) had 40 kJ, and the Shrimp (Level below that) had 400 kJ. The Algae (Base) would have had 4000 kJ.

questions.question: Cyanobacteria belong to the domain of:
questions.solution:
Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are Producers.
  • They are photosynthetic organisms that can produce their own food from sunlight and are significant contributors to the Earth's oxygen supply.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins includes cobalt as an essential component?
questions.solution:
Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) is the only vitamin that contains a metal ion, specifically Cobalt.
  • It is essential for red blood cell formation and the healthy functioning of the nervous system.

questions.question: Which structure within the nucleus contains genetic information in the form of DNA?
questions.solution:
Chromosomes are the structures within the nucleus that contain DNA.
  • During cell division, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes to ensure genetic information is accurately passed to daughter cells.

questions.question: Pellagra is a deficiency disease that usually occurs due to lack of which of the following nutrients?
questions.solution:
Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of Niacin (Vitamin B3).
  • It is classically characterized by the 'four Ds': Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia, and, if untreated, Death.

questions.question: Analgesic medicines are used for _________________.
questions.option_2: correcting deficiencies due to vitamins and nutrients
questions.option_4: killing or weakening microbes and infections
questions.solution:
Analgesic medicines are used specifically for reducing pain (e.g., aspirin, paracetamol).
  • Some analgesics also have antipyretic properties, meaning they can help reduce fever.
